clue.text: See 9
Like some big game one bungled in series

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step

parts.note: a line is a series, as in a line of kings

indicators.note: something bungled is botched, so the letters of one are jumbled

explanation.surface: A hunter fumbles one shot in a run of attempts at big game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'big game' suggests a match, but it is the hunter's prey. Leo is a papal name, part of the puzzle's theme of popes.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonine means lion-like, and the lion is the classic big-game animal.

clue.text: A fifth of money put in collection so far

indicators.note: put in means placed inside, here the letter goes inside the word for collection

parts.note: a set is a collection

indicators.note: fifth of picks the fifth letter of the word money

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a fifth of the money has gone into the collection so far.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'A fifth of money' not as a fraction but as A plus Y, the fifth letter of 'money'; Y goes inside SET.
explanation.definitionFit: As yet is an idiom meaning up to now, until this time.

clue.text: Not successfully treated, a priest abroad died

parts.note: un is French for a, and abroad covers both words
a curé is a French parish priest
D is the abbreviation for died in genealogies

explanation.surface: A priest dies overseas, his illness never successfully treated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' tells you to use French: UN for 'a' and CURE (curé) for 'priest'.
explanation.definitionFit: An illness that is uncured has not been healed despite any medical treatment.

clue.text: For example, interrupting tardy representative

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into the middle of the word for tardy

parts.note: tardy means late
EG is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: A late-arriving delegate is cut off mid-sentence with an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A legate is an envoy, especially a papal one sent to represent the Pope.

clue.text: Time to remember rising in Dublin and Rome?

definitions.text: Time to remember rising in Dublin and Rome?

parts.words: Time to remember rising in Dublin and Rome?
parts.note: the 1916 rising in Dublin began on this holiday, and in Rome the Church celebrates the rising of Christ from the dead then

explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' points to a rebellion in Dublin and to the Resurrection celebrated in Rome; one festival covers both.
explanation.definitionFit: The Easter Rising of 1916 in Ireland and the Christian feast of the Resurrection share the same name.

clue.text: A lover of priestess carrying cross for great king

indicators.note: carrying means holding something inside, so the lover's name holds the cross

parts.note: in Greek myth Leander swam the Hellespont nightly to his lover Hero, a priestess of Aphrodite
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: A priestess's lover bears a cross on behalf of a great king.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander the Great was the Macedonian king who conquered the Persian Empire.

clue.text: Prophetic text in final letter going into East European port

indicators.note: going into means entering, so the letter is placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: Kiel is a German port on the Baltic
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A prophetic message sits in the last letter sent to a port in eastern Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: Z goes in after the first E of E + E + KIEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Ezekiel is a book of prophecy in the Old Testament, named after its prophet.

clue.text: Gift I can point out — what preacher's good at

definitions.note: a noun phrase naming an activity, matching the gerund

indicators.note: out here means wrongly placed, so the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A preacher with a gift can point out his flock's faults: sermonising is his skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Pontificating means holding forth pompously, the way a preacher delivers a sermon; a pontiff is also a pope.

clue.text: Religious alliance in turbulent age he and you'll put together

indicators.note: turbulent means stormy and disordered, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: In a stormy era, two people agree to join forces in a religious alliance.
explanation.definitionFit: Holy Leagues were alliances of Catholic states formed by popes, such as the one that fought at Lepanto.

clue.text: Closed with rite in unusual order, like monks in monastery

definitions.note: an adjective phrase, matching the adjectival participle

indicators.note: the letters are set out in an unusual order, which means rearranged

explanation.surface: A closed rite in an unusual religious order, kept by monks within a monastery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' looks like a religious order in this clue, but 'in unusual order' is the signal to rearrange CLOSED + RITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloistered means secluded from the world, as monks are within the covered walks of a monastery.

clue.text: Follower of uniform writer of history?

definitions.meaning: in the NATO alphabet ... comes right after Uniform
history is said to be written by the winners

explanation.walkthrough: 'uniform' looks like clothing but is the NATO code word for U; Victor is also a papal name.
explanation.definitionFit: Victor is both the NATO code word for V and a word for a winner, who is said to write history.

clue.text: Like some puzzles in mathematics

indicators.note: in tells you the answer sits inside the letters of the following word

explanation.surface: Some puzzles are rather like problems in mathematics.
explanation.definitionFit: A thematic crossword such as this one, with its popes, is built around a unifying topic.

clue.text: Resisted leader of flock repeatedly going outside closed circle

indicators.note: going outside means surrounding, so the F letters wrap around the others

parts.note: F is the first letter of flock, taken three times here
closed means ended
O is circle-shaped

explanation.surface: A shepherd keeps circling his flock to stop wolves getting into the closed fold.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fs split around ENDED + O: one before, two after.
explanation.definitionFit: To fend off an attack is to ward it off or repel it.

clue.text: Role for Catholic woman once in charade — a con, essentially

indicators.note: in tells you the answer is concealed within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A woman plays a Catholic role in a charade, which is essentially a con.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' looks like the hidden-word signal, but it is just part of the letters the answer hides in; 'in' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A deaconess was a female church officer, a role the early Catholic Church once allowed women.

clue.text: One old-fashioned object of veneration

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: fashioned means shaped or made, so the letters of old are made into a new form

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned object of worship.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphenated 'old-fashioned' must be split: the second half is the instruction to rework the first.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is an image or person worshipped or adored.

clue.text: Caught, unlike priests — in court, sort of

definitions.note: clay is a kind of tennis court surface, used here as a noun

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
lay means not belonging to the clergy

explanation.surface: Someone is caught out, not being a priest, in a court of law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' suggests law, but it is a tennis court, as in the clay courts of the French Open.
explanation.definitionFit: Clay is one of the main surfaces for tennis, alongside grass and hard courts.

clue.text: Curate muddled about name for mythical creature

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the mixed letters go around the abbreviation
muddled means confused, so the letters of curate are mixed up

explanation.surface: A confused curate fumbles a name while talking about a mythical creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'muddled' turns CURATE into CETAUR, and 'about' puts it around N.
explanation.definitionFit: A centaur is a creature of Greek myth, half human and half horse.

clue.text: Ecstasy among RC saints confused scriptwriter

indicators.note: among means placed in the middle of the other letters
confused means jumbled, so the letters of RC saints are rearranged

parts.note: E is the slang abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A scriptwriter confused by Roman Catholic saints in ecstasy.
explanation.walkthrough: RC is the standard abbreviation for Roman Catholic, and it joins the saints as anagram fodder rather than being decoded.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenarist writes scenarios, the scripts or outlines for films.

clue.text: Name of woman the Devil upended with triumphant expression

indicators.note: upended means turned upside down, which in a down answer reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: Satan is the Devil
ha is an exclamation of triumph

explanation.surface: A woman turns the Devil upside down and cries out in triumph.
explanation.definitionFit: Natasha is a Russian girl's name, a pet form of Natalia.

clue.text: Monarch once put foot down on female party member?

indicators.note: on means placed on top of, so in a down answer the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: to step is to put a foot down
a hen is a woman on a hen party, the British pre-wedding night out for a bride

explanation.surface: A monarch once stamped down hard on a woman from a political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party member' suggests politics, but this is a hen party, the British bride-to-be's celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen was King of England in the twelfth century; Stephen is also a papal name.

clue.text: First in a certain line, second cutting in — bother!

indicators.note: cutting in means pushing into the middle of the other word

parts.note: St Peter was the first in the line of popes

explanation.surface: Someone at the front of a queue is annoyed when another person cuts in second.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First in a certain line' is not a first letter but the first pope, Peter, fitting the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: To pester someone is to annoy them with repeated requests.

clue.text: Elected with no change in Washington, pure and simple

parts.note: in means elected, as a party in power
a cent is small change in American money

explanation.surface: A politician elected in Washington with nothing changed, pure and simple.
explanation.walkthrough: Innocent is also a papal name.
explanation.definitionFit: Innocent means free from guilt and also naive or guileless, unspoiled in nature.

clue.text: Figurative expressions translated by 11, 21, and 27, say, apart from first page

indicators.note: apart from means without, so the letter is removed

parts.note: Victor, Innocent and Martin are all names of popes

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the word page

parts.note: the word page supplies its first letter

explanation.surface: Figures of speech are translated by three other answers, except on the first page.
explanation.walkthrough: The three answers named are VICTOR, INNOCENT and MARTIN, all papal names, so they are POPES.
explanation.definitionFit: Tropes are figures of speech, words used in a non-literal way.

clue.text: Ring on bishop, with gemstone, ornamental article

parts.note: O is ring-shaped
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
jet is a black stone used in jewellery

explanation.surface: A bishop's ring set with a gemstone is an ornamental piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An objet, short for objet d'art, is a decorative ornament or curio.

clue.text: A period of fasting among sources of fruit and sweeties

indicators.note: among means placed inside the other word

parts.note: vines produce grapes
Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: During a period of fasting a person sticks to fruit rather than sweets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweeties' suggests candy, but here it means sweethearts.
explanation.definitionFit: Valentines are sweethearts, the people one sends cards to on 14 February.

clue.text: American throne for English king

definitions.meaning: American slang for a toilet, jokingly a throne
King ... of England, who sealed Magna Carta

explanation.walkthrough: 'throne' is a joking word for a toilet; John is also a papal name.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both American slang for a lavatory and the name of a medieval English monarch.

clue.text: Religious aid on which one can count

definitions.text: Religious aid on which one can count

parts.words: Religious aid on which one can count
parts.note: a string of beads used to keep count of prayers, here dressed up as something dependable

explanation.walkthrough: 'count on' suggests reliability, but literally the beads are counted as prayers are said.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosary is a string of beads Catholics use to keep track of prayers recited.

clue.text: Swallow cocktail the second one's left

indicators.note: left means departed, so the letter goes from the word

parts.note: a martini is a cocktail of gin and vermouth
the second I in the cocktail's name, one being I as a Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Someone gulps a cocktail after the second drinker has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallow' looks like a verb about drinking but is the bird; Martin is also a papal name.
explanation.definitionFit: The house martin and sand martin are birds of the swallow family.
